positions.title: Software Developer (C++) - Infrastructure, Architecture & Tools
positions.description:
• Contributed to adopting CppMicroServices, an open-source C++ framework, into MathWorks codebase for deferred loading of dynamic libraries, reduced memory footprint, and improved start-up time.
• Implemented additional services in CppMicroServices to improve security and logging capabilities, following an industry-leading framework specification defined by OSGi Alliance.
• Designed and implemented macOS (finished) and Linux (in progress) code-signing infrastructures for MathWorks’ automated Build-and-Test system.
• Streamlined and updated MATLAB/Simulink File Associations infrastructure for Windows and macOS using CppMicroServices framework.

positions.title: Software Engineer (macOS) - Infrastructure, Architecture & Tools
positions.description:
• Improved the quality of MathWorks products’ integration with Apple’s macOS platform by contributing to the ongoing development of the Platform Foundation Libraries (native dialog box, string conversion, etc.) in Objective-C++.
• Developed and maintained macOS Cocoa and command-line tool applications (in Objective-C and Swift) to assist internal developers building and debugging Objective-C++ and C++ modules natively on Xcode.

positions.title: Application Support Engineer
positions.description:
• Provided application (MATLAB) support to MathWorks customers in the U.S. and worldwide. 
• Completed technical projects with a Software Development team to improve the skillsets needed to successfully transfer to a development group within MathWorks.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.locationName: Partnership for AiR Transportation Noise & Emissions Reduction (PARTNER)
positions.description:
• Utilized a Fortran-based atmospheric air quality model to estimate the health impacts of aviation emissions to assist in prospective policy decision-making.
• Designed and enhanced data processing algorithms in MATLAB to generate model inputs (meteorology and emissions).
• Reduced the computation time of model input generation by incorporating parallel computing (parfor loops) and a more efficient data importing methodology in MATLAB.
• Communicated effectively with research advisor, project managers, coworkers, and outside experts through bi-monthly presentations, weekly conference calls, and e-mail correspondence.
• Generated reports and results to fulfill requirements for research funded by the U.S. Federal Aviation
Administration, related projects, and completion of graduate thesis.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Collaborated with a graduate student to maintain and improve the Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) system based on a Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID).
• Demonstrated the SQUID MRI’s ability to capture the image contrast between healthy and cancerous prostate tissues, for publication.
